gold: Ipsilateral hemisphere hemorrhagic stroke with peripheral-type facial paralysis

selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including incomplete closure of the right eye, flattening of the right nasolabial fold, and right-sided hemiplegia, along with imaging studies showing hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region, are most consistent with a stroke, particularly given the acute onset and the presence of multiple supportive findings.

rejected.label: Corticobulbar tract lesion
rejected.why: While the corticobulbar tract appeared thinner on the left side, this finding alone does not fully explain the patient's comprehensive set of symptoms and imaging results.

rejected.label: Thalamic hemorrhage
rejected.why: Although there is evidence of thalamic hemorrhage, this is more specifically a component of the broader diagnosis of stroke, given the patient's overall clinical presentation and imaging findings.
